changes.md:
- New **Business** tab and **Part F: Business and opportunities**, to help you think commercially and prepare for a COO role:
  - 16 business lines open to a Hong Kong bank (custody, distribution, dealing, financing, staking, tokenised deposits, stablecoin roles, banking the industry, digital bonds, tokenised funds, ETF roles, collateral, trade finance, cross-border payments, advice and management, infrastructure). Each shows the bank's role, who pays, cost and capital drivers, the regulatory gate and its status, official signals and industry benchmarks. Filter by value-chain stage and client segment.
  - Six modules: F1 Where the money is; F2 How regulation writes the P&L; F3 Market structure; F4 Timing and scenarios; F5a/F5b Running the business; F6 Your path to COO.
  - Six read-through case studies with invented people and firms, each with three decisions and discussion notes.
  - A factual side-by-side of Hong Kong, Singapore (MAS) and Dubai (VARA). No ranking.
- New source types, clearly labelled: **Estimate** (industry studies), **Intl** (international bodies such as the BIS and FSB), **Foreign** (MAS, VARA) and **Filing** (listed firms' own reports). These are never presented as Hong Kong official facts. The Documents tab shows them only if you switch on "Industry & foreign".
- Purple **Analysis — not official** boxes hold frameworks for thinking. They contain no forecasts and no advice. The only forecasts on the site sit in F4's "How to read market-size forecasts" box, which shows how far estimates differ and why.
- 24 more official sources added (approvals for executives, market data, tax, digital banks). The register now holds 761 official documents.
- Every Part F page was checked claim by claim against its sources by a separate reviewer, then checked again for consistency across pages.
- All 761 document summaries rewritten in plain English: average sentence length fell from about 28 to about 18 words, and sentences over 25 words fell from about half to about 15%. Numbers, dates, locators and force words were checked automatically after every change, and a grammar pass fixed broken sentence splits.
- Modules C1–C7 now link to the matching business lines. Wide tables can be scrolled with the keyboard.

- Every module and project page was rewritten in plain English. Sentences are shorter (about 11–13 words on average; almost none over 25). Every term and abbreviation is explained the first time it appears on a page. Vague lines were replaced with direct ones.
- Facts, numbers, dates, citations and the force of each rule (must / should / may / proposes) were kept. A checker compared every rewritten page with the original. A second reviewer then read each rewrite against the original and, where in doubt, the official text. That review found and fixed 186 places where simpler wording had shifted the meaning, for example a rule stated more widely than the source, or "expects" turned into a bare instruction.
- One correction came from this review. Clients served through a general virtual-asset account still need the knowledge test even if they trade only Relevant Stablecoins (HKMA circular, footnote 4).
- The first 30 document summaries were also rewritten in plain English. The rest will follow.

- Usability fixes: shorter citation chips; the source panel now closes when you change page, keeps keyboard focus and returns you to where you were; "See in Documents" works for every citation; your document filters are no longer reset by following a citation; the Back button returns you to the same place in a list; clearer status colours (conclusions and targets are amber, not green); a tidier filter panel on phones; a "More" menu on tablets; page titles for bookmarks.

- HKDA Brief launched: 21 modules, 15 project profiles and 737 official documents, reflecting publications up to 25 Sep 2026.
- Every line was fact-checked a second time against the official text. This covered all 21 modules (about 1,750 claims, about 800 of them tightened), all 15 project profiles (each checked twice) and all 737 document summaries.
- The main corrections: "must" softened to "should" or "expects" where the source says so; exact paragraph and page references; statuses brought up to date (for example, September 2025 HKMA consultation drafts now show as superseded by the final rules in force from 1 January 2026); and the licensed-platform count fixed at 13 (SFC list, 29 May 2026).
- New tabs: Obligations (checklist), Briefings (talking points by audience), Timeline and Glossary.

Discuss tokenised products, custody and staking with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.6]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3]

Run the ML/TF risk assessment before launching any new product, new business practice or new technology. Examples of new products are a VA, tokenisation or stablecoin service. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]

Brief the board so it understands cryptoasset risks firm-wide and can set limits. Those limits sit within the bank's risk appetite (the level of risk it is willing to accept). [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8, pp.63-64]
Complete a comprehensive risk assessment before custody launch, under board oversight. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]

Monitor custody security 24/7, test system changes before deployment and monitor dependencies. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23-25]
Keep documented classification evidence for each cryptoasset exposure. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]
Take the DLT considerations into account when preparing DLT-related submissions. The HKMA encourages this. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]

Obtain HKMA consent before appointing an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer to hold the stablecoins it issues. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14] The issuer's keys must be kept in Hong Kong or a location the HKMA accepts. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14]
Document due diligence on custody delegates and HSM vendors, and review them regularly. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 11(a), 15]
Vet tokenisation platforms and staking providers before use, and monitor them afterwards. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]; [S:4641e6c404d2, section C, p.3]

Classify every VA-linked product [S:8a016a912528, paras 5–10]. Then apply the PI-only, suitability and knowledge-test rules that follow from that classification [S:8a016a912528, paras 5–10].
Carry out extra due diligence, using Appendix 4, on any VA fund the SFC has not authorised [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].
Give VA risk disclosures and warning statements to clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:8a016a912528, para 15].

Receive or withdraw client VAs only through segregated accounts [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]. Use accounts held at the partner platform or at an AI that meets HKMA custody standards [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)].

For Relevant Stablecoins, disclose material information on how the coin keeps its value and how redemption works [S:a0bd48559762, paras (5), (8), (10)]. Commission rebates or other benefits should not be the main basis for soliciting or recommending a coin [S:a0bd48559762, paras (5), (8), (10)].
Have adequate policies, procedures and controls for Relevant Stablecoin activities, and train staff [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9].

Keep Relevant-Stablecoin-only clients to Relevant Stablecoins [S:a0bd48559762, fn 4]. Apply the full rules, including the knowledge test, before dealing in any other VA for them [S:a0bd48559762, fn 4].

Keep the listed records on client VAs, staking and VA financing for at least seven years [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 9.6–9.8]. Keep records of orders and instructions on client VAs for at least two years [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 9.6–9.8].
Get a signed staking-risk acknowledgement before staking for clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.7(b), 8.8].

Monitor the volatility of VA collateral in real time when relying on it [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)]. Treat loans secured only by VAs as clean loans, meaning unsecured for capital purposes [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)]. The reason is that the Banking (Capital) Rules do not recognise VA collateral [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)].

Tell the SFC in advance, and the HKMA where applicable, about any new VA activity or change to one [S:8a016a912528, para 31]. That includes a change in the type of client served [S:8a016a912528, para 31].
Notify before the first client VA deposit or withdrawal, the first staking service, or the first VA-funded subscription or redemption [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 10].

A bank that is an AI but not an RI should follow the same standards [S:1babdb609fc8, pp.1–2]. It should discuss any Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting [S:1babdb609fc8, pp.1–2].
Report any actual or suspected material breach of the terms to the SFC and the HKMA as soon as practicable [S:31b4f67e0233, para 12.1].

Confirm that the platform holds an actual SFC licence [S:8a016a912528, para 17 and fn 20]. Some platforms are only treated as licensed under Schedule 3G of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). Those platforms do not count [S:8a016a912528, para 17 and fn 20].

Use only an SFC-licensed platform or an AI as the staking service provider [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.2–8.3]. Confirm it has SFC approval or has discussed the service with the HKMA [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.2–8.3].

For in-kind or VA-funded subscriptions, hold the VAs only at SFC-licensed platforms or AIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)]. For those transfers, comply with the VA chapter (Chapter 12) of the SFC's anti-money-laundering (AML) guideline [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)].

Apply the joint circular's selling rules when you sell any SFC-authorised VA fund [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 9]. These rules include the VA-knowledge test for all clients except institutional and qualified corporate PIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 9].

Offer complex VA-related products (products whose terms and risks a retail investor is unlikely to understand) only to PIs [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1, 12.3]. VA funds not authorised by the SFC are one example [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1, 12.3]. Before offering such a fund, do the Appendix 4 due diligence on the fund and its manager [S:8a016a912528, appendices, Appendix 4]. Cover the firms the fund uses for trading and custody too [S:8a016a912528, appendices, Appendix 4].
Be a licensed corporation or registered institution to distribute tokenised authorised products [S:58ea8520974d, para 18]. Apply the usual onboarding and suitability rules [S:58ea8520974d, para 18].

Apply the underlying product's selling rules to tokenised products that the Securities and Futures Ordinance does not cover [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. The HKMA expects this, and expects the same for tokenised deposits placed by customers [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. The HKMA also expects AIs to understand and control the extra risks that tokenisation brings [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. RIs that sell tokenised products other than tokenised securities should follow this HKMA guidance [S:d5ebca32c92b, fn 2].

Show clients the price-deviation alert if the bank acts as a Connecting Broker [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4]. A Connecting Broker is a licensed corporation or registered institution that routes clients' trades to VATPs [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4]. Tell clients they can subscribe or redeem at NAV instead [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4]. Get clients to confirm the risks before onboarding them [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4].

Keep an online screen that shows the indicative NAV and the last NAV [S:a64e364fd912, para 20(b)]. The indicative NAV is usually refreshed at least every 15 seconds while trading is open [S:a64e364fd912, para 20(b)].
Build access rights and controls into any online platform that sells VA-related products, so the platform enforces selling restrictions [S:8a016a912528, para 11].

Give the SFC advance notice before first letting clients subscribe or redeem with VAs, including in-kind flows [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 7(a), 10(d)]. Tell the HKMA too, where relevant [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 7(a), 10(d)].
Notify the SFC before first taking part in secondary trading of tokenised products [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]. The SFC reminds RIs to notify the HKMA too [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13].
Discuss with the HKMA before starting any activity covered by its tokenised-products circular [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6].

Hold VAs for in-kind flows only in accounts with SFC-licensed platforms or AIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)]. For these VA transfers, the supplemental joint circular also points to the SFC's anti-money laundering (AML) guideline [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)]. The relevant part is Chapter 12 of the guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VA service providers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)].

Do product due diligence on each VA-related product [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3]. Cover its risks and features, its target investors and selling restrictions, and its regulatory status [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].

Do due diligence on the issuer and its technology vendors for tokenised products under the HKMA circular [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4]. Cover smart-contract audits (independent reviews of the token's code) and private key management [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4]. Also cover contingency plans for the distributed ledger (the shared record behind the tokens) [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4].
Keep client assets and wallet addresses separate from the bank's own [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6].

Do not lend, pledge or otherwise use client assets as security [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6]. Three exceptions apply: settling transactions or fees the client owes the bank, explicit written client consent given in advance, or where the law requires it [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6].
Be liable for losses attributable to the bank, and hold adequate financial resources to cover them [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].

Disclose the custody arrangements to clients fully and fairly [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20]. Cover rights on insolvency, segregation, insurance or compensation, and commingling, which means mixing assets together [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20]. Also explain how forks and airdrops are handled [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20]. A fork splits a blockchain in two; an airdrop is a free token handout.
Keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage, and keep seeds, keys and backups in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8].
Train transaction signers in depth and run drills of the business continuity plan [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 3, 5].

Reconcile, or match, each client's holdings regularly against both on-chain records (on the blockchain) and off-chain records (kept outside it) [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21]. Escalate any discrepancies to senior management [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21].
Monitor security 24/7 [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24]. Cover outside dependencies such as vendors, blockchain protocols, encryption methods and shared code libraries [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24].
Discuss plans with the HKMA before launching custody, and show that the bank meets the standards [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
Discuss staking plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, Implementation, p.3].
Provide custody records to the HKMA promptly when asked [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 22].
As a general principle, delegate VA custody only to one of three types of firm [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]:
Before taking on a custodian, get independent reviews of its code [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]. Also understand how it builds and releases software [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15].
After taking on a custodian, check its security controls regularly [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]. Require it to report incidents promptly, and test its disaster recovery [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15].

For a VATP counterparty, the SFC's own custody standards are in the VATP Guidelines [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22; S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2]. Paras 10.6–10.8 cover cold storage, approved addresses and key management [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22]. Para 10.22 covers the compensation arrangement [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22]. The SFC circular 25EC44 adds detail to these [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2]. The HKMA annex points to the VATP Guidelines for reference on delegation [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 10].

Offer only licensed issuers' coins to retail clients when acting as an offeror. Offer other specified stablecoins only to professional investors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 4]
Follow the RI standards when dealing, advising or managing portfolios in Relevant Stablecoins. Follow the terms in Appendices A1 and A2 too. The HKMA expects this of all AIs. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

Disclose material information on each Relevant Stablecoin when dealing or advising. Cover its stabilisation arrangements (how it keeps its value) and its redemption arrangements (how holders get money back). [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5 and para (10), p.7]

Mark clearly the accounts of clients who trade only Relevant Stablecoins, to use the lighter rules for them. Deal in no other virtual assets for those clients. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4] Dealing in other virtual assets for a client brings back the full virtual asset rules. These include the knowledge assessment, a check of the client's understanding of virtual assets. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
Base advice on the client's use case (what the client needs the coin for), not on commission rebates. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]

Classify stablecoin holdings under CRP-1. A coin is Group 1b (a lower-risk stablecoin group) only if it meets classification conditions 1-4. Here, full redeemability means redemption within five calendar days. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2, 2.3.2]

Treat held stablecoins as debt securities outside high-quality liquid assets (HQLA), if your bank is a category 1 institution for liquidity. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] Under the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), a short-term cash stress test, the usual inflow is 0%. The bank counts no cash coming in from them. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] Under the net stable funding ratio (NSFR), a longer-term funding test, the required stable funding factor is 85%. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] An issuing bank must apply a 100% LCR outflow if the coin is redeemable within the LCR period. In effect, it assumes holders cash in every such coin. Lower rates are possible where the backing assets qualify as HQLA. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7]
RIs: notify the HKMA and SFC before any Relevant Stablecoin activity or material change. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
All AIs: discuss Relevant Stablecoin services with the HKMA first. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
Notify the HKMA when you acquire a new type of cryptoasset. Treat it as Group 2b (the highest-risk group) until the HKMA agrees its classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
Check any claimed issuer against the HKMA Register of licensed issuers. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The HKMA points the public to the Register to verify licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]

Hand custody (safekeeping) of stablecoins to a licensed issuer only for that issuer's own coins. An AI may do so only if the issuer has HKMA consent to provide that custody. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14 and fn 7]
Apply existing product-selling rules to tokenised products. Add the HKMA's tokenisation-specific expectations on top. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-3]
Apply the circular's standards when customers place tokenised deposits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1]

As a distributor of tokenised SFC-authorised products, the bank should be a regulated intermediary, such as a registered institution (RI). [S:58ea8520974d, para 18] It should also follow existing onboarding and suitability rules (checking a product fits the customer). [S:58ea8520974d, para 18]

Carry out due diligence on the product, its issuer and third-party vendors. Do it before offering the product and at intervals after. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4] Cover key management (how the keys that control tokens are kept safe) and audits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
Give customers plain-language disclosures on tokenisation risks. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section B, pp.4-5]
Meet the HKMA's digital asset custody standards if the bank holds tokenised products for customers (custody). [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section D, p.6]
Discuss plans for tokenised products with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Implementation', p.6]
Notify the SFC and the HKMA before starting digital-securities activity as an RI. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8]
Notify the HKMA as well when taking part, as an RI, in secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products. [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]
Consider the HKMA's Supervisory Incubator for DLT (optional). Banks can use it to reaffirm their risk controls before a full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]
Assess the track record of the issuer and the tokenisation platform. Also assess their controls over keys and ownership records. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]

Consider, for tokenised bonds, the product's legal status and whether settlement is final. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.4; Section B, p.5] Final settlement means a completed transfer is legally fixed and stays in place. For example, the HKMA states that a law protects the finality of CMU settlement for the Government digital green bonds. [S:4290ec1111e3, fn 2]

Offer VA financing only to securities margin financing clients. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2), p.2] Base it on the client's financial capability and the collateral the client posts. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2), p.2]
Treat loans secured solely by VA as clean (unsecured) loans for capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]
Do not repledge, reuse or pledge VA collateral as security for anything else. The only exception is enforcing it when a client defaults. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(c), p.5]

If relying on VA collateral, write down in the margin lending policy how the bank assesses VA risks. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(a), p.4] Monitor vulnerable VA exposures on an ongoing basis. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(a), p.4]
If relying on VA collateral, keep the ability to watch its price swings in real time and act promptly. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(b), p.4]
Set prudent triggers for margin calls and for stopping new advances. Act on them. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8), p.5]
Monitor withdrawals continuously. Be able to escalate and suspend withdrawals outside office hours too. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(b)]

The HKMA circular sets no separate notification step. For new digital-asset activity, the HKMA's existing expectation is that banks discuss plans with it before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body para 5, p.2]
The circular names contacts for queries, by topic. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]
Before trading on a shared order book, assess these points about the platform operators: [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 16]
Work with the partner VATP as needed on withdrawal limits and on blocking suspicious withdrawals. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(c)]
Keep a contingency plan for outages at the VATP whose prices the bank uses to value collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6), p.4]

Partner only with SFC-licensed platforms if the bank offers VA dealing. [S:8a016a912528, para 17] Either introduce clients to the platform, or trade through an omnibus account (one account that pools many clients' orders). [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
Offer VA dealing only to clients of the bank's Type 1 (dealing in securities) business. [S:8a016a912528, para 18]

Follow the SFC's guidance for VA brokers if the bank trades for clients on a shared order book and also gives retail clients access to it. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6] The HKMA expects this of RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]

Apply the SFC's safeguards for client VA withdrawals if the bank, as an RI, lets clients withdraw virtual assets. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6] These safeguards apply on top of the HKMA's e-banking and technology rules for RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6]
Re-check a platform's status on the live SFC lists before onboarding it and at each review. The lists can lag between updates. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 1]; [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section Note 1]
Tell the SFC in advance before the bank starts or changes VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31] Tell the HKMA too, where relevant. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]

Run a risk-based anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT) assessment when the bank takes VASPs as customers. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4] The HKMA says extra checks may be needed, depending on the relationship. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4] These are like the checks used in correspondent banking (where one bank provides accounts to another). [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4] They include understanding the customer's business, licensing status and AML/CFT controls. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4]

Find out, for VASPs based outside Hong Kong, whether each account is for the firm's own use or for its clients. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24] If the account serves clients, apply the correspondent-banking measures. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]

Benchmark a partner platform against the VATP Guidelines. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22] Check its token committee and its retail index test. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22] Check its 98% cold storage and its compensation cover. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22]
Ask whether the platform has fixed the gaps listed in the SFC's inspection findings. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1 and Appendix 2]
Classify every cryptoasset exposure under BCR Part 12 and CRP-1. Keep reassessing it on an ongoing basis. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 2.1.1]
Move an asset to Group 2b at once if it stops meeting its conditions or criteria. This covers any asset the HKMA agreed as Group 1a, 1b or 2a. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.3]
As a registered institution (RI), treat loans secured only by virtual asset collateral as clean (unsecured) loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]
Keep policies, staff and technology systems able to assess cryptoasset risk. Document the evidence behind each classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]
For stablecoins, keep a monitoring framework that checks the stabilisation mechanism works as intended. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.2.4]

If the bank is systemically important, track its Group 2 exposure ratio. Compare it with the 1% and 2% thresholds used in disclosure. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]
Notify the HKMA before acquiring any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
Give the HKMA classification evidence when it asks. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

For Group 1 assets, check each entity with a key role. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1] These roles are redemption, transfer, storage or settlement of the asset, and management of its reserves. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1] Confirm each entity is regulated and supervised, or meets suitable risk standards. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1] Confirm it also discloses a governance framework (its rules for oversight and decisions). [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1]
File the revised crypto items in MA(BS)1E, 3, 3A, 26, 27 and 28 on the stated schedules. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]; [S:f4e64fda4011, para 5]; [S:767a346fbcaa, para 4]; [S:527c897d3eed, para 4]
Complete MA(BS)3 Part IIIf if the bank is incorporated in Hong Kong. Include the Group 2 exposure ratio. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 1, 11]
Publish Table CAEA and Templates CAE1-CAE3 as they apply to the bank. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, pp.61-62]; [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218]

Use daily averages over the period for certain CAE1 columns. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (i), p.213] These are the Group 2a long and short columns, and the Group 2b total, long and short columns. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (i), p.213]
Run the 0.3% / 5% materiality test at each period end. The test decides which Group 2 assets need their own CAE1 row. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214]
Use the HKMA's explanatory notes, alongside the BDR, when filling in each standard template and table. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]
Agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA if your systems are not ready for the revised returns. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]

Be ready to describe, for each Group 1 asset, how the bank assessed the four classification conditions. Include the public information used. Table CAEA asks for this. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA point (f), p.211]
Complete CDD before any occasional VA transfer of HK$8,000 or more. Watch for linked transfers. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4–4.2.5]
Meet AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A for VA transfers the bank carries out. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15; S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]

Assess money laundering and terrorist financing risk before launching any VA-related product, service or new technology. Put controls in place to reduce that risk. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10–2.11; S:642680fa4467, pp.2–3]
Keep VA transfer and relationship records for the periods in para 8.4. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]
Monitor customers' flows to and from VA platforms, and look into what they are for. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
Write down the settings and thresholds that trigger transaction-monitoring alerts. Review them regularly and have them checked independently. [S:7bfdad704174, para 5.8]
In the RI business, apply SFC Chapter 12 when handling client VA deposits and withdrawals. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]
Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5]

For the RI: tell the SFC and HKMA before it starts VA activities or changes them. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] This covers dealing, advice and asset management, and changes to the type of clients served. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
File STRs with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) where the bank finds grounds for suspicion. The JFIU is the unit that receives these reports. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 5.10–5.12]
For overseas VASPs that get correspondent-like services, do the following: [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23–11.24]
Confirm with each VASP customer that its operations do not break the laws that apply in Hong Kong or elsewhere. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]

Note that the SFC expects licensed firms to register the client bank accounts used for deposits and withdrawals. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 20] It also expects them to whitelist client wallet addresses, meaning they keep a list of approved addresses. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 20]
Keep the board and senior management in charge of DLT risk. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1] Update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
For custody, run a full risk assessment before launch. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1] Make sure the board and senior management oversee the activity before and during it. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
For client VAs, meet the key-management controls in para 11 of the custody annex: [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11, fn 8]
Use system controls and whitelists to stop unauthorised transfers out of cold wallets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10] Check each transaction through a systematic process. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]
Run security monitoring 24/7. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23] Test system changes thoroughly before they go live. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23]

Add DLT-specific scenarios to continuity plans for critical functions. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 10] Examples are cyberattacks, loss or theft of keys, and forks (a split of a blockchain into two versions). [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 10]

An HKMA speech says banks should secure their own cyber basics and those of critical service providers. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 10] It also says the risks of frontier artificial intelligence (the most advanced models) should not be underestimated. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 10]
Discuss virtual asset activity with the HKMA before launch, and get its feedback on risk controls. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
SFC-licensed firms in the bank's group should promptly report material cyber incidents to the SFC. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 18]
Internet brokers or VASPs should tell their SFC case officer at once if they expect trouble meeting the July 2027 login deadline. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 23]

Before relying on a DLT network, check that its node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 5] Node operators are the parties that run the computers that keep the network going.
For custody delegates (firms the bank hands custody to), check for: [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]

A bank may delegate custody of VAs to an SFC-licensed VATP operator after due diligence. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 14–15] The SFC's own custody standards for VATP operators show what such a platform is expected to have. [S:562c0f8addce, paras 2, 7, 10, 18, 24] They include: [S:562c0f8addce, paras 2, 7, 10, 18, 24]
Map whether any group entity carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers as a business. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M] Include acting as a go-between. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
Test each such entity, including branches, against the Hong Kong link (nexus) rules. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
Plan to register by 31 January of the year after the entity first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
Plan for due diligence from 1 January 2027. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] Collect self-certifications from existing users within 12 months. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
Prepare CRS systems for amended CRS due diligence from 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)]; [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]
Keep CARF due-diligence evidence and reporting records for six years after each return's due date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
Keep oversight of any outsourced CARF work. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)] Under the bill, using a service provider would not in itself be a reasonable excuse. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

Plan to send test data files to the IRD for checking if the bank uses its own in-house software. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(c)] The consultation's timetable set the fourth quarter of 2027 for this testing. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(c)]

Note that CARF registration and returns would go to the IRD, not to the HKMA or SFC. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement'] The IRD's planned CARF Portal is the channel for them. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement'] Watch for the portal and the data schema (the technical format for the data). [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']

Note that a crypto trading platform or broker the bank partners with may itself be an RCASP with its own reporting duties. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Individuals and entities subject to due diligence and reporting requirements']

List your bank's current and planned VA dealing, custody, advisory and management activity. Firms now doing VA activities under SFC licence or registration conditions will need a licence or registration under the new regimes. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]

Plan for a fixed start date with no transition. No arrangement is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31-32, 34] Dealers that have not contacted the SFC or HKMA may have to stop operating on that date. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31-32, 34]

Note the marketing ban that applies once the regimes are in force. Firms without a licence or registration will be prohibited from actively marketing VA advisory or management services to the Hong Kong public. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 70]
Note the SFC's stated plan to launch its system for monitoring digital-asset custody in the second half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
Track the CARF start date for any group company that may be an RCASP. The bill sets that date as 1 January 2027. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]

Note that the regulators encourage firms interested in VA dealing to approach the SFC early, or the HKMA where relevant. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33] The aim is to begin pre-application talks (informal talks before a formal application). [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]

Note that existing and would-be VA advisers and managers are strongly encouraged to start pre-application talks with the SFC early. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 7] This matters if your bank gives VA advice or manages VAs, or plans to.
Under the dealing regime, check that the VA custodians holding client assets are regulated by the SFC. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]

Know the scope of the SFC's 27 May 2026 circular. It covers only Relevant Stablecoins. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2] These are specified stablecoins issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer and authorised under its licence. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2] The circular does not cover other stablecoins. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2]

On mBridge, run AML, counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and sanctions checks off the platform before sending a payment. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30] The receiving bank runs its own check before confirming the payment. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]

On mBridge, meet each jurisdiction's AML, CTF and sanctions laws. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35] The platform attaches a pass or fail certificate to each transaction, based on the bank's own off-platform check. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]
Keep KYC, AML and CTF checks in the bank's own systems, outside the mBridge platform ("off-bridge"). [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]

If the bank takes a role in distributing e-HKD, note the 2022 policy paper. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35] It said a two-tier design could give customer-facing institutions two tasks: customer due diligence (checking who customers are) and record-keeping. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]

Banks may use the HKMA Supervisory Incubator for distributed ledger technology (DLT). [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] DLT is a shared record kept in step across many parties. The Incubator lets banks reaffirm their risk controls before a full DLT launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] Tokenised deposits are a core focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

On mBridge, foreign banks can hold and use a CBDC. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, pp.31-32] Only domestic banks can swap their reserves at the central bank for that CBDC, or swap it back. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, pp.31-32] Check which role each counterparty has.

talking.md: The bank's VA conduct duties (rules on how it treats clients) apply to the bank as an RI. The HKMA supervises the bank day to day, not the SFC directly. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]

The bank must comply with the HKMA's anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT) Guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1] As an RI, it must also take into account the SFC's AML/CFT Guideline, including its Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1]
Any new VA product needs an HKMA discussion before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5] RIs must also tell the SFC and HKMA in advance. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
Only two stablecoin issuers are licensed. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The Government says any further licences would keep the total very limited. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]
The Government proposed that the SFC lead licensing for VA dealing and custody. The HKMA would be the banks' frontline regulator. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
No arrangement is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply when these regimes start. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

The Basel cryptoasset standard applies from 1 January 2026. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.4.1-1.4.2, 2.1.2] Until the HKMA agrees the bank's classification, two things stay in Group 2b: exposures held before that date and any new cryptoasset type. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.4.1-1.4.2, 2.1.2]
The HKMA's custody annex expects banks to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]
Our AML Guideline says *should* is mandatory, the same as *must*. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
Check each SPM module's classification. SB-1 is statutory; CRP-1 is a guidance note that gives way to the BCR. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
Conclusions papers are not law. The FSTB and SFC aim to put a dealing bill into LegCo in 2026. [S:6186c01c6649, p.4, Next step]
The Budget said the same for the dealing and custodian regimes. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]
The conclusions state no plan to treat existing firms as licensed while they apply. They encourage early talks with the SFC or HKMA. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 33-34]

Hong Kong rules move from consultation to conclusions, bill, start date and transition. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] For stablecoins, consultation began on 27 December 2023. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1] The Ordinance started on 1 August 2025, about 19 months later. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
Planned bills in the Budget are stated intentions, not obligations. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]
LegCo's negative-vetting period for the cryptoasset capital rules expired without extension. The rules apply from 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, paras 1-2]
HKMA letters can change how capital guidance applies with immediate effect, as one did in June 2026. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]

The 2026 licensing regime is still only a target. The bill has yet to go to LegCo. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22] By contrast, the business-model circular already sets a board expectation for every authorized institution. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
The government now says *digital assets*, but AMLO still says *virtual asset*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]; [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1]

The SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] It will also promote their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
EnsembleTX is to add CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]

The HKMA sees a chance for banks to link traditional finance and digital assets as a key intermediary. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2] It expects a board-endorsed plan. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2]
The government's stated 2026 target is a bill to license digital-asset dealing and custody. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22]

The Blueprint's Quantum Preparedness Index measures how ready banks are for post-quantum cryptography. [S:b0607b779270, para 4] Post-quantum cryptography is encryption built to resist future quantum computers. The first index reading was 2.3 out of 10. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
ASPIRe may shift custody rules toward outcome-based standards. That idea is still exploratory. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]
Our VA conduct rules apply to us because we are an RI. The HKMA supervises us; the SFC keeps ultimate responsibility. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]

Check who each paper covers. The May 2026 Relevant Stablecoin circular is addressed to RIs. The separate stablecoin letter covers all AIs. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
As an RI, we should tell the SFC and HKMA when we plan to start or change VA services. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
Under the proposed custodian regime, the SFC would regulate a custody subsidiary. The HKMA would be frontline regulator for the bank itself. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
Under the proposed dealing and custody regimes, the SFC would license and register providers. The HKMA would be frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
The MA can withdraw or suspend an executive officer's consent for misconduct. Each regulated activity must always have at least one executive officer available. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 6.3]
A bank VA custodian would use existing HKMA capital rules, not the custodian capital floor. [S:f41a543388bc, para 41]
The RI financing circular requires loans secured only by virtual assets to be treated as clean (unsecured) loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

Every new VA, tokenisation, custody, staking or stablecoin launch starts with an HKMA discussion. [S:642680fa4467, p.5] For RI activities, the SFC and HKMA also expect advance notice. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]

The 2026 custody letter dropped the six-month confirmation. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] Existing custodians should review and revise their controls instead. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
We talk to the HKMA before go-live on any new digital-asset activity. The March 2026 circular restates that step. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]

We should flag a new client type to the SFC in advance, and to the HKMA where relevant. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10] The same goes for our first VA deposits, staking or VA-funded subscriptions. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
The HKMA asked each board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
The Supervisory Incubator gives us a dedicated HKMA team for feedback before a full DLT launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Live trials there are optional. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]
We must notify the HKMA when we acquire a new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] The asset sits in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees with our classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
Equity-like tokens count as shares for the 5%-of-Tier-1 consent test. [S:13365a31e794, fn 1]
The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline requires an ML/TF risk assessment before any new product, practice or technology launch. In that guideline, "should" is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11]
The DLT considerations are non-binding. Even so, the HKMA encourages banks to take them into account in DLT-related submissions. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]

As a general principle, we can outsource VA custody only to another AI, an SFC-licensed platform, or a licensed stablecoin issuer. A stablecoin issuer qualifies only for the coins it issues, and only with HKMA consent. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
Before we offer tokenised products to customers, we need due diligence on the issuer and its technology vendors. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]

The HKMA expects the board to understand cryptoasset risks. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8] It also expects the board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4]
If our capital or risk management for crypto falls short, the HKMA may consider capital add-ons, provisioning or limits. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

For custody keys, the HKMA looks for HSM devices, a Hong Kong location and sharding. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8] It also looks for no blind signing (approving unseen details) and 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8]
DLT continuity plans should test key loss, cyberattacks and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]

The regime reaches us as an RI through conditions the SFC puts on our registration, consulting the HKMA where applicable [S:8a016a912528, para 19; S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]. The HKMA is our frontline, day-to-day supervisor [S:8a016a912528, para 19; S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3].

Our AML baseline is the HKMA AML Guideline [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 fn 1]. As an RI we are also required to take into account the VA chapter (Chapter 12) of the SFC guideline [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 fn 1].

SFC-authorised VA funds are not PI-only, and retail clients can buy listed ones on SEHK [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 6.2, 9, 9.1]. We should still assess VA knowledge first. Overseas VA exchange-traded products that are not derivatives remain PI-only [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 6.2, 9, 9.1].

Since May 2026, clearly ring-fenced Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no knowledge test and no exposure limit [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (3)]. The coin must come from an HKMA-licensed issuer [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (3)].

The regulators relaxed parts of the regime in December 2023, September 2025 and May 2026 [S:8a016a912528, para 9; S:d5ebca32c92b, para 2; S:a0bd48559762, Background]. Complex-product rules, knowledge tests and licensed venues remain [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.2, 17].
In January 2026 the SFC fined a broker HK$4 million for VA distribution failures from 2018 to 2022 [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–2].

Margin clients can get VA financing [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5]. Only bitcoin, ether and Relevant Stablecoins count as VA collateral, with at least a 60% haircut on bitcoin and ether [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5]. VA collateral gets no capital recognition [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5].
Discretionary VA exposure under Type 1 should stay below 10% of the client account's GAV [S:31b4f67e0233, para 4.7].

The VA fund circular is written for product providers [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 8, 19, 27]. Our duties as distributor or participating dealer come from the joint circular and any extra SFC terms for PDs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 8, 19, 27].
For secondary trading of tokenised products, intermediaries notify the SFC first [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]. RIs are reminded to notify the HKMA as well [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13].

Retail clients can trade SEHK-listed VA ETFs on exchange without a suitability check if we did not solicit or recommend the trade [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14]. They still need a knowledge test [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14]. Unlisted classes of the same fund need a full suitability check [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14].

In-kind creation is allowed, and the VAs may come from overseas holdings [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18]. PDs are expected to move the VAs into custody at VATPs or AIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18].

Hong Kong allowed futures-only VA ETFs in 2022 and spot VA funds in 2023 [S:51dac2cabe78, para 12; S:5b6530666cc2, para 5]. Fund staking followed in 2025 [S:353535602a83, para 27]. In 2026 came a pilot of 24/7 secondary trading of tokenised funds [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4].
As of March 2026, 13 tokenised products held about $10.7 billion in their tokenised classes [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 3].
VA funds should not use leverage for VA exposure at fund level [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 15, 20]. Custody can go only to VATPs, qualifying AIs, or firms the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 15, 20].

Staking by funds needs SFC consultation and approval first [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(f), 31]. Interim and annual reports should show staked holdings as a share of NAV, along with revenue and costs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(f), 31].

The 2026 annex replaced the 2024 one. Existing services should review and revise their systems and controls to meet the latest standards. The letter sets no transition period [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].

The custody annex no longer has an AML/CFT section [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]. But the cover letter reminds AIs to comply with all applicable requirements [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]. The HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline sets the standards AIs should meet [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3].
With HKMA consent, a bank may now delegate custody of a licensed stablecoin to its issuer [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14(iii)].
Transfers to third parties for payments and settlement are now allowed if effective controls are in place [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m)].

Fixed insurance percentages are gone [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. In their place, the bank is liable for losses attributable to it, backed by adequate financial resources [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8].

The FSTB and SFC conclusions propose a custodian licence set by law [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]. The conclusions give existing providers no right to carry on while they apply. Banks the HKMA has already assessed get a faster process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].
The SFC says weaknesses shown by overseas cybersecurity incidents can arise whichever custody solution is used: HSM, MPC or multi-signature [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].

The HKMA lists slashing, lock-up periods and validator inactivity among staking risks to disclose [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B]. A validator is a node that checks blockchain transactions. The bank should keep control of the means to unstake [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B].
Banks are permitted offerors. Only licensed issuers' coins may be offered to retail investors. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]; [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]
RIs notify the HKMA and SFC before Relevant Stablecoin activity. Other AIs discuss it with the HKMA first. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]

Two issuers hold licences, effective 10 April 2026. The HKMA says any further licences would keep the total very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, Follow-up work section, para 3]

Relevant-Stablecoin-only dealing is not limited to RIs registered for Type 1 (dealing in securities). Clearly marked Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no virtual asset knowledge test. The Appendix A1 conditions still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, paras (2), (3)(a)]
A bank can apply to issue stablecoins. The minimum criteria on financial resources and business activities do not apply to AI applicants. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.2.1; fns 1, 8]
In June 2026 the Government expected the first regulated stablecoin launch as early as mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)]

For liquidity, a held stablecoin counts as a debt security that is not HQLA. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7] An issuing bank must apply a 100% LCR outflow if the coin is redeemable within the LCR period. Lower rates are possible with HQLA-eligible backing. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]

HKMA-licensed coins can be treated as meeting CRP-1's extra measures for permissionless blockchains (public networks anyone can join). They still need conditions 1-4 to reach Group 1. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.6.3]
Existing product rules apply to tokenised products. The HKMA adds expectations on due diligence, disclosure and early discussion with it. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-6]

As an RI, the bank should tell the SFC and the HKMA before digital-securities work. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, fn 8] It should also notify the HKMA before secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products. [S:a64e364fd912, fn 13]

EnsembleTX is to run throughout 2026 with real-value tokenised-deposit settlement. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3 and CE remarks] The HKMA invites parties with real-value tokenised-deposit use cases to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3 and CE remarks]

The DBGS Full Grant pays up to HK$2.5m per issue. It is not available if the DLT platform provider is an associate of the issuer. [S:5a0563de8142, ss.1, 3] A Half Grant of up to HK$1.25m may still apply. [S:5a0563de8142, ss.1, 3]

The Government has made three tokenised bond issues. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] The latest raised about HK$10bn. [S:ac6cd085a325, para 1] The HKMC priced a digital bond of about HK$12bn in June 2026. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]
The Policy Address targets CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation for EnsembleTX around end-2026. It also targets a CMU OmniClear digital asset platform this year. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(iv), 50]

Tokenised deposits the bank issues cannot get stable-deposit treatment in the LCR. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] If the bank cannot always identify the holders, it must treat them as "other unsecured wholesale funding". [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4]

The HKMA's April 2024 DLT risk considerations are not binding. They cover network choice, smart contracts (code that runs by itself on a ledger), legal risks such as settlement finality, and third parties. They also cover interoperability (systems working together), cybersecurity and private-key security. [S:1884530ff235, Introduction and items 2-8]

Under the HKMA's circular of 27 May 2026, our bank, as an RI, can offer VA margin financing. The condition is that we observe standards similar to the SFC's. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(4), pp.2-4] If we rely on VA collateral, it should be only bitcoin, ether or stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(4), pp.2-4]
The withdrawal and shared-order-book standards come from SFC circular 26EC5, paras 15-20. The HKMA applies them to RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]
Only securities margin financing clients qualify. Their limits are not expected to rise just because VA financing exists. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3), p.2]
Retail clients can use a shared order book only after a prominent explanation of the overseas risks and their express opt-in. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 17]
The SFC calls this a first step to bring margin trading into VA. The aim is more liquidity in a risk-controlled setting. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 3]
The Banking (Capital) Rules give VA collateral no recognition. So loans secured solely by VA are treated as clean loans. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]
Bitcoin and ether collateral should get a haircut of 60% or more. For stablecoins, the HKMA asks only for a prudent haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), footnote 5, pp.3-4]

The HKMA notes that VAs have a short track record in major market-wide shocks. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3), closing paragraph, p.3] Even the most traded VA has fallen sharply within a day and over several days. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3), closing paragraph, p.3]

The VATP Guidelines bind platforms, not the bank. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2] We use them as a due diligence benchmark, because our VA dealing must run through SFC-licensed platforms. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]

For customers that are VASPs, we follow the HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24] That includes correspondent-banking-style checks on overseas VASPs. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]

Platforms can now share order books with SFC approval. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26] They can also use affiliated market makers after notifying the SFC. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, para 9] The SFC's framework says perpetual contracts should go to professional investors only. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
If we trade for clients on a platform's shared order book and give retail clients access to it, the HKMA expects us to follow the SFC's broker guidance. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]

From 2019 to 2020, Hong Kong platform licensing was opt-in and for professional investors only. [S:024089b01825, para 32]; [S:60682e9fd7fa, Note 1] Since June 2023, every platform in or marketing to Hong Kong has needed a licence. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
The SFC's licensed list showed 13 platforms at 29 May 2026. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]

The Guidelines say licensed platforms should keep 98% of client virtual assets in cold storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22] Their compensation cover should equal 50% of cold-stored and 100% of hot-stored client assets. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
The SFC's inspections of applicants treated as licensed covered cybersecurity, client assets and KYC. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] The SFC said platforms should fix gaps at once. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]
The capital rules are law from 1 January 2026. CRP-1 is guidance, and the BCR wins if they differ. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]
We need to tell the HKMA before we acquire any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

A new cryptoasset sits in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees its classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] That means a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), pp.214-215] With the 8% minimum total capital ratio, 1,250% × 8% = 100%, so the bank holds capital equal to the whole exposure. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 2.1.2]
Stablecoins under the HKMA licensing regime can be treated as meeting the permissionless-blockchain safeguards. The four classification conditions still apply. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.6.3]
Hong Kong's rules started on 1 January 2026, matching the Basel timetable. [S:277820235891, closing para]
The HKMA can override our classifications. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6] It can also add capital or limits if it sees weaknesses. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]
Any crypto exposure ends our small-amount exception from the market risk capital rules. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80]

For a category 1 institution, a stablecoin it holds is generally not HQLA. It counts as a 0% inflow under the LCR. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 7] The net stable funding ratio tests that long-term assets have stable funding. Under it, the stablecoin has an 85% required stable funding factor. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 7]
Crypto reporting started on 1 January 2026. The transition window for banks with no crypto ended on 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
CA-D-1 is general guidance on the HKMA's approach. If it conflicts with the Disclosure Rules, the Rules prevail. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

A Transition AI that picked up crypto exposure after 1 January 2026 was grouped with exposed banks. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4] If its systems were not ready, it could agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4]
The public CAE1 narrative shows the total market value of crypto we hold in custody for clients, split by type. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]
If we have crypto exposures, our public Pillar 3 report has a crypto section. It has a yearly narrative plus numbers twice a year. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, pp.61-62]
Seven HKMA returns changed at once for the cryptoasset standard. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
Every Hong Kong-incorporated AI reports its Group 2 exposure ratio in Part IIIf. Only global and domestic systemically important banks report the add-on. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
Tokenised deposits do not get stable-deposit outflow rates in the liquidity return. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]

Our main AML text for VAs is the HKMA Guideline for AIs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3, fn 1] Our RI business must take SFC Chapter 12 into account, and comply with it for client VA deposits or withdrawals. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3, fn 1; S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]
For our own VA transfers, the Guideline points to AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A, not the wire-transfer chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15]
Any VA product needs a written money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment. [S:7bfdad704174, para 2.11] It also needs a conversation with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
If we serve an overseas VASP like a correspondent bank, we need correspondent-style checks and senior management approval. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23–11.24]
The HKMA has said the AMLO does not prohibit AIs from making VA transfers for customers if they meet the section 13A requirements. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
The Government told LegCo that money involved in VA-related crime reached HK$4,398 million in 2023. That was up from HK$824 million in 2021. [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]

The SFC's red flags for licensed firms include deposits and withdrawals with little or no trading. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 7] Another is a new eDDA setup followed by whitelisting a new wallet address. [S:cfc4a0d9f1be, para 11]
An SFC circular notes that the FATF published a report on stablecoin and unhosted wallet risks on 3 March 2026. [S:00c9fbd119bf, p.3 item (3)(c)]
The SFC circular on OTPs is addressed to internet brokers and VASPs, not the bank. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1] Our own custody baseline is the HKMA custody annex. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11]
Several wallet controls in the HKMA's 2026 custody annex use the same wording as the SFC's 2025 custody circular. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11; S:562c0f8addce, Sections II–III]

Custody keys are to be kept in Hong Kong, in tamper-resistant devices such as HSMs. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(c)] Smart contracts are ruled out for cold wallets on public blockchains. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(c)]
Counterparty platforms and internet brokers are expected to move client login and device binding off OTPs by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]
The HKMA places responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks with the board and senior management. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
Phishing made up 57% of security incidents reported to HKCERT in 2025, as cited by the SFC. [S:724f4d9f786e, fn 5]
The HKMA's first quantum readiness score for the sector is 2.3 out of 10. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11] The objective is full readiness by 2030. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]

The HKMA has warned about crypto firms presenting themselves as 'banks'. [S:19c8611c621a, para 2] It has also warned about tokens falsely linked to licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:275e7319a841, para 2]

The CARF bill had its First Reading on 3 June 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] If passed, CARF duties would start on 1 January 2027, and amended CRS duties on 1 January 2028. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
Using a vendor for CARF work is not, in itself, a reasonable excuse for failing to register, check customers or report. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]
Offering crypto exchange services to customers as a business could make an entity an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M] That is true even when it only acts as a go-between. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]

New crypto customers will need to give a tax-residence self-certification. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements'] Existing customers will need to give one within 12 months of the start date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] It targets first data exchanges from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
The government linked CARF to Hong Kong's reputation as a financial centre. [S:ab980a841782, para 3]

Under the bill, fines could add up. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A failure that continues after conviction could cost HK$500 a day. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A due-diligence breach could instead cost HK$1,000 per affected user or controlling person. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]
The consultation proposed that entities in both regimes report crypto proceeds under both CARF and CRS. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.17]

All four VA regimes for intermediaries now have conclusions, and one bill is targeted for 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] No arrangement is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63]
For dealing and custody, banks register with the SFC, and the HKMA is their frontline regulator. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]; [S:27d27650e820, para 1.10]
VA management will have no small-amount exception. A manager will need a licence or registration even if VAs are only a small share of a portfolio. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68]
Under the SFC framework, VATP perpetual contracts may take HKMA-regulated tokenised deposits as margin collateral. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']
The HKMA plans central bank money settlement and 24/7 operation for EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
CMU OmniClear is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]
C&ED aims to launch its digital-asset transaction analytics system, DATAS, by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]
The FATF's next VA/VASP update and its DeFi report are approved but not yet published. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]
mBridge leaves AML and sanctions screening to each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
The 2022 e-HKD policy paper said a two-tier design could task customer-facing institutions with customer due diligence. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]
The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale payments, to support tokenisation and cross-border payments. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
In Phase 2, commercial banks leaned slightly towards tokenised deposits over e-HKD. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Executive Summary, p.2]
mBridge reached MVP in June 2024. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1] The Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
The HKMA has not decided to issue a retail e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

The 2022 mBridge pilot ran on one central cloud system in Hong Kong. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33] The pilot report said holding the data in a single cloud raised privacy concerns. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33]

In Phase 2, privacy tools using zero-knowledge proofs were tested on public blockchains. A zero-knowledge proof shows a fact is true without revealing the data behind it. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', p.30] These tools made transactions up to 320 times more costly in gas fees, the fees paid to process each transaction. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', p.30]
Digital bonds issued in Hong Kong made up nearly 50% of the global market from 2025 to mid-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35]
Tokenised retail products held HK$10.3 billion at end-June 2026. [S:c24d834af185, Highlights, p.6]
We may deal in virtual assets only through SFC-licensed platforms. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
The HKMA expects talks before any new digital-asset activity starts. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
Licensed stablecoin issuers are required to place reserve assets with banks in Hong Kong. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (1)]
The DBGS covers half of an issuer's eligible costs, up to HK$2.5 million per issue. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2]
The HKMA may change the VA collateral haircut after notice. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), pp.3-4]
The Basel crypto-asset capital standards have applied to Hong Kong banks since 1 January 2026. [S:100b982aadca, p.90]
Basel crypto capital rules have been in force in Hong Kong since 1 January 2026. [S:100b982aadca, p.90]
The HKMA expected each board to endorse a strategic business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
We must notify the HKMA before we acquire any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
Under the SFC's AML guideline, VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more must carry fuller sender and recipient details. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5-12.11.10]

Group 2b cryptoassets on our own books take a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215] The minimum total capital ratio is 8%. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 2.1.2] So 1,250% × 8% = 100%: capital equals the exposure.
The HKMA expects us, as custodian, to be liable for client asset losses from incidents attributable to us. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
An issued stablecoin redeemable within the LCR period means a 100% assumed outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
Tokenised deposits with unknown holders count as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
Hong Kong had 13 licensed trading platforms at end-June 2026. [S:c24d834af185, p.30] The HKMA register of 23 April 2026 lists two stablecoin issuers. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
One licensed issuer is a joint venture that includes Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) Limited. [S:193316443831, para 1]
For VA dealing we may partner only with SFC-licensed platforms. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
The SFC says applicants on its list are not licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Applicant list and notes]
Planned rules would make VA dealers use SFC-regulated custodians. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
The HKMA requires licensed stablecoin issuers to place reserve assets with banks in Hong Kong. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (1)]
Licensed platforms may now pool orders with overseas affiliates. [S:8e1426ec511f, p.64, 'Increasing market accessibility']
Neither licensed issuer had issued a regulated stablecoin as of 28 April 2026. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]
The Government aims to put one bill for four VA regimes to LegCo in 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (3), 'In addition' para]
The HKMA plans 24/7 EnsembleTX with central bank money settlement by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
The Government and the SFC do not plan to treat existing VA dealers as licensed while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31] The regime takes full effect on its start date. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]
The SFC expects internet brokers and SFC-licensed VA trading platforms to adopt phishing-resistant login and device binding by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 5, 21(c)]

In June 2026 the Government said the first regulated stablecoins were expected to launch between mid-2026 and the second half of 2026, based on the issuers' plans. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, opening para]
HKEX aims to pilot tokenised warehouse-receipt financing with designated banks in 2027. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 46(iv)]
The SFC plans AML surveillance under CrypTech in 2027. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
Crypto tax reporting would start on 1 January 2027 if the bill passes. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]
The HKMA expected our board to endorse a strategic plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
Under the planned custodian regime, banks already assessed for VA custody and already providing it are to get faster licensing. [S:f41a543388bc, para 51]
We should discuss any new VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5]
As an RI, we give seven business days' notice before stopping a regulated activity. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.1]
Group 2b cryptoassets on our own books take a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215]
Buying a stake worth 5% or more of Tier 1 capital needs HKMA written consent. [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1]
A new type of cryptoasset stays in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees otherwise. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
The HKMA may consider capital add-ons or limits if our crypto risk management falls short. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]
Outsourced custody still leaves ultimate responsibility with us. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 19]
The HKMA expects custody security monitoring 24/7, holidays included. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23]
A material failure of systems and controls triggers notice to both the SFC and the HKMA. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
We need at least two EOs for each regulated activity, with one always available. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9]
The HKMA expects us not to launch until staff understand the product, its market and its rules. [S:6ea96c41cccc, para 3.7.4]
Stopping a regulated activity needs at least seven business days' notice. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.1]
The HKMA expects us, as custodian, to be liable for client losses from incidents we cause. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
Where DLT supports critical functions, continuity plans should test key loss, cyberattacks and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]
The HKMA expects our board to endorse, within six months of 9 March 2026, a strategic plan for DLT and related tech change. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
The HKMA expects us to discuss any new digital-asset activity with it before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
Each regulated activity needs at least two EOs, each with HKMA consent. [S:2baef0f142a0, paras 23-24]
The HKMA treats compliance as no less important than front-office roles when naming responsible people. [S:17871e6ed4e0, Q4/A4]
The HKMA expects us not to launch a product until staff understand it and its rules. [S:6ea96c41cccc, para 3.7.4]
The SFC fee to add a regulated activity to our registration is HK$23,500 per activity. [S:13f2903631f6, para 8.4.1]
The HKMA says manager appraisals should not give undue weight to profit; they should also weigh compliance. [S:7e7494d80711, para 4.1.7]
Anyone involved in managing our regulated-activity business is subject to the SFC's disciplinary powers. [S:932ceff44493, p.2]
ASPIRe is a roadmap. Its initiatives take effect through separate SFC circulars and guidance, so track those. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 5]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2]

Items delivered so far include staking, shared order books, VA financing and perpetual contracts for professional investors. [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]; [S:f09e57feb89b, para 2]; [S:089ec86e2407, paras 2-3]
The SFC's Executive Director of Intermediaries called the roadmap-based approach essential to scaling Hong Kong's digital asset market. [S:089ec86e2407, para 5]

The SFC still frames custody standards based on results as something to explore. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] But its August 2025 custody circular to VATPs took effect immediately. [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7]
The bill is not yet law. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] If passed, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]
A customer crypto exchange service run as a business can make the entity an RCASP. This applies even when the entity acts as an intermediary. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024, with first data exchanges targeted from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]

Proposed fines can scale. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] Some continuing offences carry a further HK$500 a day after conviction. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] For due-diligence offences, the fine is the higher of two amounts: a level 3 fine, or HK$1,000 per affected user or controlling person. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A level 3 fine is a set point on Hong Kong's scale of fines.
Sela and Aurum were research projects. Sela's report says it reflects no HKMA policy decision on an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'; S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5]
About 80,000 e-CNY wallets were registered by end-January 2026. 18 Hong Kong banks support FPS top-ups. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]
Under the 2026 Shanghai MoU, the parties will explore electronic bills of lading under Project Ensemble. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
Pilot e-CNY wallets do not allow person-to-person transfers. They cap balances at RMB 10,000. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2, pp.1-2]
No rules are out yet for the platform or the Exchange Fund Bills tests. Both are stated targets. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
The platform is meant to be a one-stop service for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]
The HKMA plans tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by end-2026. This is to help banks use more than HK$1.3 trillion of these bills round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
A DLT platform has statutory finality only if the HKMA designates it. Otherwise, finality rests on contract. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 37-38, p.15]
The grant is a subsidy. The HKMA reserves the absolute right to decide eligibility and the amount. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]
Clients can recover half of eligible expenses, up to HK$2.5 million per issue. Each issuer, with its associates, can do this for two issues at most. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2]
The 2026-27 Budget says the HKMA will use the scheme to encourage more digital bond issues in Hong Kong. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97]
An issuer that uses a DLT platform provided by its own associate cannot get the Full Grant. The Half Grant is then the most it can get. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
The Evergreen report says existing SFO licensing and offering rules also apply to digital bonds. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11]
