Sixteen financial institutions arranged the HKMC deal, and settlement fell from T+5 to T+3 (five business days to three). Investors could use existing CMU links to Euroclear and Clearstream, two international settlement systems. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 5, 8]
The Policy Address says Hong Kong-issued digital bonds took nearly half the global market from 2025 to mid-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35]

The Evergreen report notes that the new capabilities of DLT platforms are largely untested in financial markets. It suggests continuity plans, including for a move to another platform. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 47, p.17]

No decision exists to introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] The 2022 paper saw the firms that distribute e-HKD as the ones that could handle customer due diligence. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]
The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale payments, supporting tokenisation and cross-border settlement. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]

The Government's November 2025 digital green bonds offered settlement in e-HKD and e-CNY (the Mainland's digital renminbi). No digital bond offering anywhere had offered this before. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money' paragraph]
In Phase 2, privacy tools called zero-knowledge proofs made transactions up to 320 times costlier in gas fees (network transaction fees). [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', PDF p.34]

EnsembleTX is a pilot, not a rulebook. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1] Customer tokenised deposits still fall under the HKMA's tokenised-products circular, which expects early discussion with the HKMA. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1; 'Implementation', p.6]

The pilot starts with tokenised money market funds and real-time treasury uses. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2 and 5] The HKMA invites proposals for new real-value uses of tokenised deposits. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2 and 5]
The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA plans 24/7 operations and CBDC settlement for EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]

Tokenised deposits cannot get the LCR treatment for stable retail deposits. If holders cannot always be identified, they count as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, p.89]
On mBridge, AML and sanctions checks stay with each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30; s.7.2(d), p.35]
Participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees for mBridge payments. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
Project mBridge reached MVP in June 2024. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1] The Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
The 2022 pilot ran on a single central cloud in Hong Kong. The report says keeping data in one cloud raised privacy concerns. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33]
The Government now says *digital assets*. But *virtual asset* is still the defined term in AMLO. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]; [S:7395a53cc85a, Note]

The 2026 Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms. It will also promote their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
The Government's stated 2026 target is one bill for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management licensing. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
Customs plans a system to analyse digital-asset transactions by 2029. The system is part of the Customs anti-money laundering big-data platform. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]

As a registered institution, we follow the HKMA circular to RIs. Circular 26EC26 sets standards for VATPs and LCs. [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph and fn 2, p.1] RIs are still reminded to notify both regulators in advance. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]

Clients with Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no VA knowledge test. They also need no VA exposure limit (cap on a client's VA holdings). Offering those clients any other VA brings back the full rules. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)-(b) and fn 4, pp.4-5]
The Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms. That includes their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
Only coins issued under an HKMA licence qualify. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] The HKMA register lists the licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 4]

Only coins from licensed issuers may be offered to retail investors. AIs are permitted offerors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1] The HKMA register lists who is licensed. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]

Two issuers hold licences that took effect on 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The HKMA says any further licences will stay very limited in number. [S:193316443831, 'Follow-up work', para 3]
An AI may apply to issue coins. The financial-resources and business-activities criteria do not apply to it. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.2.1; fns 1, 8]

A licensee must give holders a right to redeem at par. It should process valid requests within one business day. Reserves should be held under trust arrangements with qualified custodians (firms that safekeep assets). [S:240be6833157, paras 2.5.2, 2.5.4, 3.3.1, 3.3.3]
The HKMA decides any supervisory flexibility in the Incubator case by case. It depends on how the bank manages trial risks. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2]
The HKMA says six banks have launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]
The HKMA's business-model circular says a bank's strategic plan may factor in small real-world trials through the Incubator. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
The HKMA's DLT considerations say the board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
Phase 1 changed no law. It confirmed the current rules are flexible enough and added Companies Registry FAQs on DLT registers. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 6]
Phase 2 will explore signing tokenised bond issue documents electronically. The goal is a more efficient and automated issuance process. [S:279f10054c6e, para 10]
The HKMA set up the TBEG to explore policy measures, market practices and innovations with industry. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2]
Possession and transfer of tokenised instruments are topics for the phase 2 review. That review is set for H2 2026. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 8, 11]

All four regimes now have conclusions, and one bill is targeted for 2026. There are no plans to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]; [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63]
Each of the four activities will need a licence or registration once its regime starts. VA management has no small-amount exception. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 63]
Start dates are not set yet. The Government and SFC will weigh how long the market needs to adjust. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
Under the dealing regime, the SFC will require client VAs to be held with custodians the SFC regulates. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]

timeline.ev: The HKMA starts its e-HKD work with Project LionRock: a wholesale test with Hong Kong's three note-issuing banks.
The SFC says tokens sold in an initial coin offering (a crypto fundraising) may be securities under the SFO.
The HKMA publishes its second whitepaper on DLT, after the first in 2016.
An HKMA keynote speech argues that crypto-currencies such as Bitcoin do not do the job of money, and calls them crypto-assets.
The SFC sets standards for VA portfolio managers and fund distributors, covering portfolios aiming to put 10% or more in VAs.
The HKMA and the Bank of Thailand start Project Inthanon-LionRock with ten banks.
The SFC, in a position paper, offers opt-in licensing to platforms that trade security tokens, with 98% held in cold storage.
The HKMA issues a circular on the ML/TF risks of VAs and VASPs, replacing its 2014 letters.
The HKMA and the Bank of Thailand publish the Inthanon-LionRock report.
The FSTB opens an AML consultation proposing licensing for VASPs, which closes on 31 Jan 2021.
The SFC licenses the first VATP, for professional investors only.
The People's Bank of China Digital Currency Institute and the Central Bank of the UAE join, and the project becomes m-CBDC Bridge.
The FSTB concludes that VA exchanges are to be SFC-licensed and, at first, serve professional investors only.
The HKMA launches Fintech 2025, which includes a study of the e-HKD.
The HKMA begins its study of a retail e-HKD (one for the public).
The HKMA and the BIS Innovation Hub run Project Genesis, a test of tokenised green bonds.
The HKMA and its mBridge partners publish an interim report on faster, cheaper cross-border payments.
The HKMA's e-HKD technical whitepaper explores a two-tier design (central bank plus banks), and the HKMA says it is not a blueprint.
The HKMA issues a discussion paper on crypto-assets and stablecoins, with comments due by 31 Mar 2022.
The HKMA sets out its approach to AIs' dealings with VAs and VASPs.
The SFC and HKMA issue their first joint circular on VA activities.
The HKMA publishes an e-HKD policy and design paper, with comments due by 27 May 2022.
The mBridge partners begin a six-week pilot with real money, running to 23 Sep 2022.
The HKMA's paper 'e-HKD: Charting the Next Steps' sets out the three-rail approach.
The mBridge pilot report shows 20 banks in four jurisdictions, over 160 transactions and more than HK$171 million.
The HKMA and the BIS Innovation Hub publish the Project Aurum report on a two-tier retail CBDC prototype.
The FSTB's Policy Statement on VAs adopts the principle 'same activity, same risks, same regulation'.
The HKMA launches the e-HKD Pilot Programme.
LegCo passes changes to the AMLO that create VASP licensing, in force from 1 June 2023.
The HKMA circulates the Basel prudential standard (global bank safety rules) for cryptoasset exposures.
The HKMA's stablecoin consultation conclusion proposes compulsory licensing for key stablecoin activities.
The Government offers a HK$800 million tokenised green bond.
The SFC consults on rules for VATPs, including access for retail investors.
The HKMA starts e-HKD pilots with 16 firms.
The SFC's VATP conclusions allow retail investors in, with safeguards.
The HKMA revises its AML/CFT Guideline for AIs, setting a HK$8,000 threshold for VA transfers.
The AMLO licensing regime for VATPs and the SFC's VATP Guidelines take effect.
The HKMA reports on bond tokenisation in Project Evergreen.
The HKMA, the Bank of Israel and the BIS Innovation Hub publish the Project Sela report.

timeline.ev: The SFC states that no JPEX group entity is licensed by it or has applied for a licence.
The SFC publishes lists of VATPs, including applicants, and a list of suspicious VATPs.
The SFC and HKMA revise the joint circular, and the HKMA forms a CBDC Expert Group.
The HKMA publishes the e-HKD Phase 1 report and an mBridge update.
The SFC's circular on tokenised securities replaces its 2019 statement on security token offerings.
The SFC and HKMA issue the current joint circular, and the SFC issues a circular on VA funds.
The FSTB and HKMA consult on rules for stablecoin issuers, until 29 Feb 2024.
The HKMA issues CP 24.01 on banks' cryptoasset exposures, with comments due by 6 May 2024.
The Government offers about HK$6 billion of digital green bonds in several currencies.
The FSTB consults on licensing OTC VA dealers, with Customs as the licensing body.
The HKMA issues circulars on custody standards and on tokenised products; the custody guidance was replaced on 27 May 2026.
Deadline for VATPs already operating to apply for a licence if they want to be treated as licensed while the SFC decides.
The HKMA unveils Project Ensemble.
The HKMA launches its stablecoin issuer sandbox.
The HKMA announces e-HKD Phase 2.
The HKMA sets out risk-management considerations for DLT.
The HKMA forms the Ensemble Architecture Community.
The HKMA expands the cross-boundary e-CNY pilot.
From this date, VATPs in Hong Kong must be SFC-licensed or treated as licensed while they apply, as the grace period is over.
mBridge reaches minimum viable product stage (a first working version), and the Saudi Central Bank joins as a full participant.
The Banque de France and HKMA announce wholesale CBDC work under a new MoU, linking the Banque de France's platform (DL3S) to the Ensemble Sandbox.
The FSTB and HKMA publish stablecoin consultation conclusions, after 108 submissions.
The HKMA launches the Ensemble Sandbox.
The HKMA starts e-HKD Phase 2 and renames the project e-HKD+.
The HKMA sets up CMU OmniClear Limited.
The HKMA announces tie-ups with Banco Central do Brasil (Drex) and the Bank of Thailand (Project San).
The HKMA launches the Digital Bond Grant Scheme.
The Government publishes the Stablecoins Bill in the Gazette, and the Bill gets its First Reading in LegCo on 18 Dec 2024.
Hong Kong commits to CARF, the crypto tax data-sharing standard.
The SFC revamps VATP licensing, using conditional licences.
The HKMA launches its Supervisory Incubator for DLT.
The HKMA informally consults the banking associations on cryptoasset capital rules, intending them to apply from 1 Jan 2026.
The SFC publishes the ASPIRe roadmap.
The HKMA and SFC each issue circulars on staking.
LegCo passes the Stablecoins Bill.
The FSTB issues Policy Statement 2.0, built around LEAP.
The FSTB and SFC consult on VA dealing and custodian licensing, until 29 Aug 2025.
The HKMA's cryptoasset rules on capital, disclosure and exposure limits are published in the Gazette.
The Stablecoins Ordinance and the HKMA's stablecoin guidelines take effect.
The HKMA issues version 4 of SB-1.
The SFC and HKMA's supplemental joint circular lets LCs and RIs offer staking and trade through SFC-licensed platforms' off-platform services.
The Government says mBridge is part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure.
The HKMA publishes the e-HKD Phase 2 report and gives priority to wholesale uses.
The SFC issues circulars on shared liquidity and wider product offerings, and the HKMA launches Fintech 2030.
The Government offers about HK$10 billion of digital green bonds, the first digital bond offering to settle using e-HKD and e-CNY.
The HKMA launches the EnsembleTX pilot.
The HKMA issues CRP-1, effective from 1 Jan 2026.
The FSTB and IRD consult on CARF and the amended CRS, until 6 Feb 2026.
The FSTB and SFC publish conclusions on VA dealing and custodian licensing, and consult on VA advisory and management.
The Basel cryptoasset rules and CRP-1 take effect.
The SFC lets VA brokers offer VA margin financing and permits affiliated market makers. It also sets a framework for VATP perpetual contracts for professional investors.
The Budget plans a 2026 bill on VA dealing and custodian licensing, and a CARF amendment bill in the first half of 2026. It also plans a CMU OmniClear digital asset platform.
The HKMA, the Shanghai Data Bureau and the National Technology Innovation Center for Blockchain sign an MoU on digitised cargo trade and finance.
The HKMA expects each AI's board to endorse, within six months, a strategic business plan for digital transformation.
The HKMA grants the first two stablecoin issuer licences.
The SFC sets a framework to pilot secondary trading (resale after issue) of tokenised SFC-authorised products.
The Government publishes the CARF bill in the Gazette, and introduces it into LegCo on 3 Jun 2026.
The FSTB and SFC publish conclusions on VA advisory and VA management.
The HKMA issues updated custody guidance, VA financing guidance and a Relevant Stablecoin circular for RIs, and the SFC issues its own Relevant Stablecoin circular.
The SFC's list shows 13 licensed VATPs.
The HKMA clarifies para 2.6.4 of CRP-1, with immediate effect.
The HKMA convenes a Tokenised Bond Expert Group.
The FSTB and HKMA's first-phase review finds the law flexible enough for tokenised bond issuance. The next phase is to start in the second half of 2026.
The SFC gives VATPs and internet brokers 12 months to bring in phishing-resistant login and device binding (tying accounts to known devices). Its circular states this as an expectation.
The Policy Address says the HKMA is to test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end. The HKMA also plans to bring CBDC settlement and round-the-clock operation to EnsembleTX by around end-2026.

glossary.def: A bank or other institution that the HKMA has authorised. The HKMA's anti-money laundering guideline (its AML/CFT Guideline) sets the standards AIs should meet, including AIs that are also RIs. The HKMA issues that guideline under s.7 of the AMLO and s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance.

An AI that the SFC has registered to carry on one or more regulated activities (types of securities business, such as dealing or advising). The HKMA supervises RIs day to day, as frontline supervisor. Ultimate responsibility stays with the SFC.
A firm that the SFC has licensed to carry on regulated activities. The joint circulars cover LCs and RIs together, calling both 'intermediaries'.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Hong Kong's banking regulator. Among its other roles, it grants licences to stablecoin issuers under the Stablecoins Ordinance.

The Securities and Futures Commission, Hong Kong's securities regulator. It licenses VA trading platforms. The Government proposes that the SFC lead licensing and standard-setting for VA dealing and VA custody (safekeeping).
The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, the government bureau for financial policy. It issued Policy Statement 2.0. It runs the VA licensing consultations jointly with the SFC.

The body that supervises a firm day to day. This is the HKMA's proposed role for banks under the coming VA dealing and custody regimes. Under these regimes, the HKMA would supervise banks, while the SFC sets the standards.

A chapter of the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual (its supervision handbook). It covers how the HKMA supervises RIs' regulated activities. It is a statutory guideline, issued under s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance.
A person who directly supervises a regulated activity at an RI. The RI appoints this person with the HKMA's written consent. Each activity needs at least two.
The legal term for crypto and similar digital tokens. The AMLO defines it in s.53ZRA. Policy Statement 2.0 (June 2025) says the Government will now say 'digital assets' instead.

A broad term in the HKMA's custody guidance. It covers VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets (assets recorded as digital tokens). It also covers the keys, seeds and backups (the secret codes that give access) used to reach those assets.

A business that provides VA services, such as trading or transfers, to customers. The HKMA expects banks to assess each VASP customer's ML/TF risk on its own facts. That assessment includes extra due diligence (deeper checks) where needed.

An online platform where people buy and sell VAs. In SFC usage, it is a company licensed under the SFO for Types 1 and 7 (dealing in securities, and automated trading services). A company holding an AMLO VA service licence also counts.
A platform that may keep operating while the SFC decides its licence application. It was operating before 1 June 2023 and met the conditions for this status. It is not licensed and may never be.
A grace period of 12 months, from 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2024. VATPs already running, with a genuine Hong Kong presence, could operate during it. Doing so did not breach the AMLO licensing rule.
A company that holds a VATP's client assets on trust (for the clients, not for itself). It is a Hong Kong subsidiary wholly owned by the VATP. It does no other business.
Keeping the keys to VAs offline, away from the internet. The SFC expects VATPs to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage.

Cover that repays clients if their VAs are lost. A VATP should hold an SFC-approved arrangement of this kind. It should cover potential loss of 50% of client VAs in cold storage. It should also cover 100% of those in hot storage (kept online) and other storage. For bank custody, the HKMA's May 2026 guidance instead expects the bank to be liable to clients and to have adequate financial resources.
An institution, or a wealthy person or firm, that meets a legal test. The SFO defines the term in Schedule 1, Part 1, s.1. Any other person is a 'retail client'.

An investment product whose terms and risks are hard for a typical investor to understand. It triggers the SFC's complex-product rules. These include a suitability check (whether the product fits the client), even if the firm did not solicit (actively offer) the sale. The joint circular says VA-related products are very likely complex.
A notice from the SFC and HKMA together on intermediaries' VA activities. The December 2023 version replaced the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. A supplement followed in September 2025.
Locking a client's VAs into a proof-of-stake network to earn rewards. In such a network, holders who lock up tokens help check and confirm transactions.

One pool of buy and sell orders shared by an SFC-licensed VATP and an overseas platform in its group. Every order is fully pre-funded (paid for up front). Trades settle delivery-versus-payment: the asset and the payment change hands together.

A contract that tracks a VA's price, uses leverage (borrowed exposure) and has no end date. Under the SFC's February 2026 framework, licensed VATPs may propose to offer them. They should be offered to professional investors only.

glossary.def: Regular payments between the two sides of a perpetual contract. One side gains if the price rises (long) and the other if it falls (short). The payments keep the contract's price near the spot (current market) price. The SFC expects settlement at least once every 24 hours.

The rule that sender and recipient details travel with a transfer. For banks, the HKMA Guideline sets customer due diligence (checks on the customer) for one-off VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more. It points to AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A. RIs must also take into account the VA parts of Chapter 12 of the SFC AML Guideline.

A VA wallet (software or hardware) through which the owner holds and moves VAs, keeping the private key (the secret code that moves the VAs). The HKMA's May 2025 consultation proposed a check by licensed stablecoin issuers. They would check whether each customer's wallet is custodial (run by a provider) or unhosted.
A public SFC list of suspicious trading platforms. It helps the public spot suspicious platforms doing business in Hong Kong.

Dealing in VAs (buying and selling them) as a business. The June 2025 proposal covers this business in Hong Kong. It runs from simple conversion (swapping one asset for another) to brokerage and block trades (very large deals). Banks would register with the SFC, with the HKMA as frontline regulator.

Keeping VAs safe for others as a business. Under the December 2025 conclusions, it means holding, for others, the private keys or similar tools that can move VAs. Trustees or managers that only hand custody to someone else are out of scope.

Advising clients on VAs, and managing VA portfolios for them. Both are proposed licensing regimes. Their scope will match the SFO regimes for advising on securities (Type 4) and asset management (Type 9).
Letting firms already in business carry on under a new regime, as if licensed, while they apply. None is planned for the VA dealing or VA custodian regimes.
A faster route to approval. It is promised for SFC-licensed VATPs. It is also promised for LCs and RIs that already provide VA dealing services.

A technology firm that splits control of a private key among several parties. Whether it needs a custodian licence depends on the facts of each case. The main tests are whether it can move client VAs on its own, and whether clients can always reach their assets independently.

A scheme to license OTC VA trading businesses. The February 2024 proposal was for the Commissioner of Customs and Excise to license spot VA trading (buying and selling for immediate delivery). The proposal also covered shops and crypto cash machines. The June 2025 dealing proposal revised the scheme.
Hong Kong's stablecoin law. Stablecoins are tokens designed to hold a steady value. The law set up licensing for regulated stablecoin activities and came into force on 1 August 2025.

A stablecoin whose value is tied to one or more fiat currencies (ordinary government-issued money). An HKMA licence is needed to issue one in Hong Kong as a business. A licence is also needed to issue one tied to the Hong Kong dollar as a business, in or outside Hong Kong.
A stablecoin issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer under its licence. It is a 'specified stablecoin', a category set out in law.
The HKMA's public list of licensed stablecoin issuers. The HKMA keeps it under s.21 of Cap. 656.

A controlled space where would-be stablecoin issuers could test their plans with the HKMA. The HKMA launched it in March 2024 to share its supervisory expectations. Admission was not an HKMA endorsement. Participants had to apply separately for a licence.

In the bank capital rules, a digital form of value. It relies mainly on cryptography (code-based security) and DLT or similar technology. It can be used to pay, to invest, or to access goods or services.

Classes of cryptoasset treated like the traditional asset behind them. Group 1a is tokenised traditional assets. Group 1b is stablecoins with effective stabilisation mechanisms (ways to keep the price steady). Both carry the same capital requirements as the underlying traditional asset. An infrastructure add-on (an extra charge for technology risk) may apply on top.

Cryptoassets with the toughest capital treatment. They are unbacked cryptoassets, and tokenised assets or stablecoins that fail the classification conditions. They are fully capitalised: a 1,250% risk weight times the 8% minimum total capital ratio means the bank holds capital equal to the whole exposure [S:5d0c13e09312, para 2.1.2]. Limited hedging (offsetting positions) is recognised for 2a, and none for 2b.
The HKMA's guidance on sorting cryptoassets into these groups. It is non-statutory (not issued under a law). If it differs from the Banking (Capital) Rules, the Rules prevail.

LegCo's 28-day review of subsidiary legislation (detailed rules made under an existing law). The amendment rules on cryptoasset capital, disclosure and exposure limits completed this review in August 2025.
A commercial bank deposit in digital token form. The bank itself issues it.

A digital token version of a real-world investment product, recorded on DLT. In HKMA usage, it covers products not regulated under the SFO, and excludes stablecoins. The sales rules for the underlying product generally apply to its tokenised form too.
A traditional security, such as a share or bond, wrapped in a digital token. The SFC judges whether it is complex by looking through to the underlying security.
A digital token that stands in for cash. In Project Evergreen, the CMU minted (created) each token as a claim on the HKMA for one Hong Kong dollar.

A bond issued first in the normal way, then turned into tokens on a DLT platform. In Project Evergreen, the CMU made its book entries first. The investors' beneficial interests (ownership rights) were then recorded on the ledger.

CMU: the Central Moneymarkets Unit, a bond settlement system. CMU OmniClear: the company that runs it for the HKMA. The HKMA owns the CMU. CMU OmniClear Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Exchange Fund (Hong Kong's official reserves), set up in October 2024.
An HKMA grant for issuing digital bonds in Hong Kong. It pays up to HK$2.5 million per eligible digital bond issue. It is open for an initial three years from November 2024.
An HKMA arrangement that lets banks check their DLT risk controls before a full launch. Banks can choose to run live trials.

Distributed ledger technology: a database shared and copied across many computers, such as a blockchain. The HKMA's non-binding considerations expect an AI's board and senior management to take full responsibility for DLT risks.

CBDC: central bank digital currency, meaning money a central bank issues in digital form. The e-HKD is the HKMA's possible digital Hong Kong dollar, for wholesale and retail uses. The HKMA currently gives priority to wholesale use (between banks and other financial institutions).
Central bank digital money used for settlement between banks. It is the basis of Project Ensemble.
The new name for Project e-HKD from September 2024. The project widened from the e-HKD alone to new forms of digital money, including tokenised deposits.
The HKMA's three-part path for the e-HKD. Rail 1 lays the foundations. Rail 2 covers use cases and pilots. Rail 3 covers implementation planning.
Project Ensemble: HKMA work on settling deals in tokenised money. EnsembleTX: its pilot phase using real money, from November 2025.
A group the HKMA formed in May 2024. Its members are regulators, banks and technology firms. It develops industry standards so that systems can work together (interoperability).
A shared platform for cross-border payments in several central banks' digital currencies. It settles payment-versus-payment (both currencies swap at once), in real time, 24/7.
Doing compliance checks outside the mBridge platform. Banks meet each jurisdiction's KYC and AML/CFT rules off the platform.

PvP: payment-versus-payment. DvP: delivery-versus-payment. In PvP, two payments in different currencies settle together. In DvP, an asset and its payment settle together. The Ensemble Sandbox was built to test both for settlement between banks. The SFC describes DvP as a simultaneous exchange of assets that lowers the risk of one side not delivering.
Settling both sides of a deal at the same instant. Each side depends on the other.

Money with rules attached about how it can be used. It works as a 'wrapper' that sets conditions while leaving the underlying value intact. Phase 2 pilots examined it as an alternative to a natively programmable e-HKD (one with rules built into the money itself). A natively programmable e-HKD could weaken fungibility (every unit being interchangeable).
In Project Sela, a new type of go-between that serves retail CBDC users directly. It handles tasks such as onboarding and KYC. It does not hold users' CBDC or its own liquidity (cash reserves).

A basic personal wallet for the digital renminbi. It is opened with a Hong Kong mobile number, without real-name checks. The balance is capped at 10,000 renminbi. It allows retail payments only, not person-to-person transfers.
Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF): an OECD standard for tax authorities to swap crypto-asset tax data automatically each year.

RCASP: a reporting crypto-asset service provider. HKRCASP: an RCASP that meets a test of its link to Hong Kong. Under the 2026 Bill, an RCASP is a business that carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers.

CRS: the Common Reporting Standard. AEOI: automatic exchange of information. The CRS is the OECD model for swapping financial account information automatically each year. Hong Kong has run it since 2018.

Reporting financial institution (RFI): a financial institution that reports account data under the CRS. Under the amended CRS, these institutions report gross proceeds (total sale amounts) from sales of relevant crypto-assets by default.
Specified electronic money product (SEMP): a type of e-money product. CARF leaves it out, but the amended CRS brings it in.
An independent appeal body. Under the 2026 Bill, an RCASP could appeal to it against a CARF financial penalty assessment.
DATAS: the Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System. AMLAS: the Anti-Money Laundering Analytics System. Both are data-analysis systems the Customs and Excise Department has planned (by 2029).
An SFC technology initiative. Its big-data tools for watching markets and for AML surveillance are to switch on in 2027.
A regular FATF report on how countries apply its standards for VAs and VASPs. The sixth was published on 26 June 2025.
Activities with the same risks get the same rules, whatever form they take. The Government has applied this principle to VA activity since 2022.
The four focus areas of Policy Statement 2.0. LEAP stands for Legal streamlining, Expanding tokenised products, Advancing use cases, and People and partnerships.
The SFC's 2025 roadmap, with 12 initiatives. ASPIRe stands for its five pillars: Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure and Relationships.
The HKMA's financial technology strategy, with over 40 initiatives. Its four pillars are data and payments, artificial intelligence, resilience, and tokenisation.
